title: Correlation properties of heart rate variability to assess the first ventilatory threshold and fatigue in runners
authors: Van Hooren B, Mennen B, Gronwald T, Bongers BC, Rogers B
population: 14 individuals running a treadmill session with two incremental ramps, using a consumer-grade chest belt
findings: First ramp: bias between gas-exchange VT1 and DFA-a1 0.75 was -0.5 ml/kg/min (95% limits of agreement -6.8 to 5.8) for VO2 and -0.9 bpm (-12.2 to 10.5) for HR; R2 0.83 and 0.56.
Second ramp: bias -7.3 ml/kg/min (-18.1 to 3.5) for VO2 and -12.3 bpm (-30.4 to 5.9) for HR; R2 0.62 and 0.43.
The authors state individual-level accuracy was similar to that of gas-exchange methods and that DFA-a1 only accurately demarcates thresholds in a non-fatigued state.
limitations: Small sample (n = 14); treadmill only; individual limits of agreement of about +/-11 bpm are wide; no long-term or race-condition validation. Published online 2023-11-02, print January 2025 (vol 43).
implications: Use DFA-a1 0.75 HR only from fresh, non-fatigued efforts and attach an error band of about +/-11 bpm (first-ramp limits of agreement); do not update zone boundaries from sessions late in a long or fatigued run.
A DFA-a1 0.75 crossing at a markedly lower HR than the stored VT1 HR can be logged as a possible fatigue signal; no automatic plan change is justified from one study.

verification.notes: Crossref: J Sports Sci vol 43 pp 125-134, online 2023-11-02, print 2025-01-17 (Europe PMC lists year 2025; kept 2023 as first publication). Abstract confirms all numbers. Design relabelled to other (within-session two-ramp comparison). 'Similar to gas exchange methods' rewritten as the authors' statement.
